newsitem.title: USA: DEC holders hope for new board nominees.
newsitem.headline: DEC holders hope for new board nominees.

text.p: A group of institutional shareholders who own about 30 to 40 percent of Digital Equipment Corp stock met in New York late Wednesday to discuss alternatives for the beleaguered company in light of its poor financial and stock performance.

Herbert Denton, president of broker/dealer Providence Capital Inc, said that he hopes the next step for the shareholders will be to arrange a meeting with Digital's nominating committee of its board of directors.
The goal is to replace three board members who are up for re-election in November, not including Chairman and Chief Executive Robert Palmer.
Denton told reporters after an almost two-hour meeting that he does not yet have any replacement candidates in mind.

"The first step would be to meet with the nominating committee," Denton said, adding that over the next day or two he will begin telephoning all of the institutions represented at the meeting and determine their interest in writing a letter, requesting a meeting with Digital's nominating committee.

"We have to see what the reaction is," Denton said, adding that many of the shareholders at the meeting agreed that one of Digital's key problems is that it lacks marketing skills, despite its technological prowess.

Denton said that in the past his company has participated in getting new directors nominated to the boards of several companies, but he would not venture to nominate someone from Providence to the Digital board.
Denton would only say that he owns "a very small stake" in Digital.
Several experts participated in the meeting, including an intellectual property lawyer, marketing consultants and Wall Street analyst John Jones of Salomon Brothers.
About 70 people attended the meeting, with 50 in the audience and the rest on the telephone.
Denton said that Palmer is indeed under a great deal of pressure. He said that if Digital's financials do not improve soon, the board will likely begin to question Palmer.
